fridgeAlchemy

Not a restaurant. Not a cookery school. A different way of thinking about food and what happens when people gather around it.

Scroll

"You don't need a recipe for every occasion. You need curiosity, a well-kept larder, and the confidence that what's in your fridge right now is enough to make something worth eating."

The fridgeAlchemy philosophy

Where this came from

An experienced cook.
No chef's hat.

fridgeAlchemy didn't start as a business idea. It started as a question, "what's in the fridge?"

The question was asked when we had a supper to create without having thought ahead and I found I was able to create something that turned out delicious. My son Jack, who grew up with this experience, told me recently that he never thought about food any other way - that everything on a plate was always just different ingredients to him, not a finished thing to be received. That is what fridgeAlchemy is trying to share.

No Michelin ambitions. No formal training. Twenty-one years running a consultancy, a decade of fell running and exploring nature and the outdoors in the Welsh mountains, and the conviction that the place we inhabit and the landscape around us holds everything we need to eat well.

Imagined in the Black Mountains and Monmouthshire

What this is actually about

fridgeAlchemy is not a showcase. The food is never the point on its own — it's the thing that makes the conversation happen, that gets people into a kitchen together, that connects what's on the plate to the landscape outside the window.

Some evenings guests are invited to send a photo of their fridge and larder before they arrive. The meal is partly built around what they already have at home. That's not a gimmick — it's the whole idea. Food as autobiography. The kitchen as a space for participation, not performance.

The community comes first. Everything else follows from that.

Four ways in

Two are free.
Two are bookable.
All are open.

fridgeAlchemy moves across four pillars. Foraging and movement will be free, weekly, and for anyone. Kitchen and Retreats are where the venture sustains itself — and where the ideas come to life most fully.

01

Kitchen

Supper evenings and hands-on workshops from a Monmouthshire kitchen. Guests cook alongside, not in front of. The meal comes from what's available — local, seasonal, honest. We start our menu planning with vegan and gluten free as standard, and will add some items that are vegetarian, with-gluten and non-vegetarian where it fits.

Before each evening, guests are invited to send three pictures — their fridge, their larder, their view outside. These arrive at the table as a small printed booklet, with questions, space for notes, and the evening's recipes. Something to keep.

Beyond the table

Open the fridge door.
Step through.

fridgeAlchemy starts with a simple question — what's in the fridge? — but it doesn't stop at the fridge door. Look out of the kitchen window: a garden, a hedgerow, a neighbour, a farm down the lane. The fridge is really your way into the food that's close to you, and what you do with it starts a conversation.

At a fridgeAlchemy table we cook from what's here, and we talk — about where food comes from, who grows it, what it means in our families, what we'd want to pass on. Everyone has an opinion and nobody needs to be an expert. Over a shared meal, people say things they wouldn't say in a meeting.

It isn't a purist philosophy. If you need to buy something from the supermarket, that's fine. It's a direction of travel, not a rulebook. Whatever the setting, there is one communal table, for up to 25 people, with no stage and no audience. There's always enough to start a conversation.

Questions we might start with

What's in your fridge, your larder, and outside your window?

Who grows or makes the food you eat — and do you know their name?

What does food mean in your family, and what would you want to keep?

A supper table

Up to 25 people, one table

A shared meal built from the fridge, the larder and the view outside the window, with conversation woven through it. In a kitchen, a barn or a pub.

A kitchen workshop

Half a day, hands-on

Cooking together around one ingredient, one technique or one idea, and using it to talk about where food comes from and who we want to be around it.

Facilitation

For groups and organisations

I design and lead food-led conversations for communities, schools, festivals and teams, shaped around your people and your place.

If you'd like to bring a fridgeAlchemy conversation to your community, school or team, I'd be glad to talk it through. There's no obligation.

The fridgeAlchemy Network

Become a Fridgealchemist

The question — what's in the fridge? — works anywhere. In a kitchen in Monmouthshire, on a hillside somewhere, or at a table in your own home, wherever that is. If the idea resonates with how you already think about food and community, we'd like to help you build it where you are.

Your kitchen, your people

fridgeAlchemy events happen in real kitchens — domestic, unhurried, a little imperfect. Everything about how you run yours, including any commercial arrangements, is yours entirely.

Tools, not rules

We'll share what we've learned — event formats, hosting guides, the fridge-and-larder invitation, and the booklet template. That booklet — guests' three pictures, prompt questions, notes space, and the evening's recipes — is one of the most distinctive things fridgeAlchemy does. It travels with the idea.

A community of practice

Connect with others running fridgeAlchemy evenings in different places. Over time, the booklets from different kitchens become a distributed record of how the idea lives in different hands, different landscapes, different larders. That's the network.

The network is coming soon.

To register your interest and tell us where you are, email me at spriestnall6@gmail.com or message me on WhatsApp.
